Can Africa turn SDG 7 ⚡️progress into Agenda 2063 transformation fast enough to leave no one behind?
 
Electrification across Africa rose from 51 percent in 2017 to 61 percent in 2023, giving more than 120 million people access to electricity, with Northern Africa near universal access and strong gains in Eastern and Western Africa.
 
Yet the gaps remain stark: more than 560 million Africans still lack electricity, and over 940 million lack clean cooking. In many communities, energy poverty is still felt as household smoke, fuel collection time and health burdens borne mainly by women.
 
I was pleased to contribute to the Affordable and Clean Energy session at the Twelfth Africa Regional Forum on Sustainable Development in Addis Ababa, where we discussed the opportunities on how SDG 7 can accelerate the 2030 Agenda and Agenda 2063.
 
The question is no longer whether Africa has ambition. It does. The question is how we move from targets to investment, delivery and transformative impact.
 
Three shifts are critical.
 
⭐️First, sustainable energy must become an industrialisation agenda. Africa has about 60 percent of the world’s best solar resources, but only a small share of installed solar capacity. Algeria’s 15 GW solar target by 2035 and Morocco’s Noor Ouarzazate solar complex show what is possible.
 
⭐️Second, clean cooking must move to the centre of energy planning. Kenya’s clean cooking strategy and electric cooking pilots in Mozambique and Sierra Leone show how it can be linked to electrification, tariff reform and national power systems.
 
⭐️Third, leverage data and digital intelligence to make delivery visible and measurable. Ethiopia’s satellite-integrated electrification planning and Mozambique’s use of electrification and socio-economic data show how better targeting can support mini-grids and e-cooking.

UNDP continues to support countries with geospatial tools and energy planning models, including the Clean Energy Equity Index, so policies are tracked against delivery and investors have clearer signals.
 
If countries get their decisions right, SDG 7 and Agenda 2063 can become one delivery agenda for smarter planning, stronger institutions, better investment and impact at scale.
